presentation: Fallout 1/2-like overhead oblique/trimetric CRPG art study; exact engine projection not specified

tests.reference_role: architectural and material reference; camera and surface treatment transformed
tests.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer
Asset type: LCL / The Hush gameplay-oriented environment ideation, overhead test A.
Input image: architectural and material reference only. It shows the station's piers, separate freight corridor, closed passenger gate, dispenser, relay terminal, bench, overhead freight crane, and lone waiting adult. Completely change camera and rendering treatment as requested below; do not preserve its photographic perspective.
Primary request: reimagine this same station as a convincing classic Fallout 1 / Fallout 2-style 2.5D CRPG environment. FIXED ELEVATED THREE-QUARTER OBLIQUE/TRIMETRIC GAME CAMERA, near-parallel projection. It should read like a richly detailed prerendered-sprite RPG playfield with no UI, not a cinematic painting or modern miniature diorama. The camera looks down over a playable station area. Object sizes stay constant across distance; receding lines remain parallel. Do not force perfectly symmetric true-isometric diamonds.
Scene: a continuous railway-station level filling the entire rectangular frame, extending beyond all edges. Visible ground plane, tiled concrete concourse, freight rails and a serviced trolley to one side, closed passenger barrier at a pier, adjacent dispenser and relay, a worn bench on the passenger side, repeated concrete structural supports and a service stair/gallery. The same freight handling crane and cargo load are visible as compact sprite-like industrial forms with controlled occlusion. Hide the roof and shorten near walls using classic CRPG interior visibility conventions; this is a cutaway presentation, not a destroyed building.
Readability: the closed gate, waiting person, bench, terminal, and active machine route must be distinguishable at normal game zoom. Human sprites are small, approximately 5 percent of total image height, with realistic adult proportions and crisp silhouettes. One ordinary adult in a worn work coat and small tool bag waits outside the gate. No portrait close-ups or giant foreground person. Keep clear walking routes and enough empty concourse to allow later human occupation.
Style/medium: textured prerendered 3D-to-2D sprite aesthetic of late-1990s CRPGs; deliberate low-resolution character and prop forms, crisp clustered material detail and subtle dithering, realistic volume, consistent directional contact shadows. Detailed but modest fidelity: not photorealistic camera rendering, not smooth plastic 3D, not hand-painted fantasy, not chunky Minecraft voxels. Preserve LCL's European municipal industrial design, not Fallout's American retrofuturist world.
Condition: clean operational freight machinery and contact surfaces beside neglected passenger furnishings and a closed amenity. Selective local stains and wear, no universal rust. Diffuse daylight translated into readable baked lighting; sparse cold-white task lamps and tiny cyan indicators. Muted concrete, civic paint, worn wood, metal.
Framing: wide landscape game-screen composition. Screen-filling continuous environment, no visible horizon, no sky, no distant vanishing point, no giant arched photographic vista, no black void or white studio around a floating floor slab.
Avoid: lens blur, cinematic perspective, dramatic god rays, fog, bloom, rainy reflections dominating the scene, neon wash, giant holograms, fantasy aura, toy proportions, pedestal or dollhouse display, title, labels, captions, UI, logos, borders, watermark. This is camera/readability ideation, not an engine-exact map.

Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: LCL / The Hush overhead CRPG station study B.
Input image: edit target, new overhead station A. Preserve the exact fixed elevated oblique/trimetric camera, near-parallel projection, image dimensions, floor tile axes, character scale, pier positions, galleries, stair, freight tracks, crane, containers, dispenser, relay terminal, and gate housings. Preserve the textured prerendered-sprite-like classic CRPG appearance. No camera shift or cinematic transformation.
Primary request: add a modest Patchwork Republic human occupation to this same overhead playfield, preserving clear routes and a separate immaculate autonomous freight corridor.
Changes: organize a compact communal repair workbench on the accessible left side near the stair landing, with neatly arranged tools, fitted replacement parts, clamp silhouettes, and a modest amber task lamp. Give the lower-left existing bench a few carefully fitted timber replacement slats and an embroidered cushion, retaining its silhouette and exact position. Place a small domestic table alongside it, with a kettle and two distinguishable cup forms, a modest potted plant, and a small personal decoration. Show a neatly fitted drainage or floor repair around the occupied corner, slightly cleaner and drier than the neglected floor outside it. Show skill and affection rather than clutter or an indiscriminate orange wash.
People: keep the original adult waiting near the closed gate with the same clothing and tool bag. Add two compact adult game-character sprites matching the original person's scale and realistic proportions: one works at the repair bench, another sits at the restored passenger bench. No close-up faces or oversized heroes.
Readability: occupied work and rest areas read as clear grouped silhouettes at reduced size. Small decor supports these groups; it does not overwhelm the tile grid. Walking paths remain open. The gate remains closed so machine exclusion is still visible.
Constraints: keep architecture and camera unchanged; additions stay on the human concourse. Muted industrial materials, local warm light, small cyan machine indicators, directional contact shadows. No photographic lens effects, horizon, blur, dense microclutter, fantasy objects, magic, neon fog, miniature dollhouse framing, floating ground slab, new buildings, UI, captions, labels, logo, border, watermark.

Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: LCL / The Hush overhead CRPG station study C.
Input image: edit target, overhead station B. Preserve the exact fixed elevated oblique/trimetric camera, near-parallel projection, image dimensions, tiled floor axes, pier geometry, gallery and stair, tracks, freight crane and cargo, gate housings, wall food dispenser and relay, repaired bench and domestic table, potted plant, organized workbench, warm task lights, and all character identities. Preserve the classic textured prerendered-sprite-like 2.5D CRPG treatment and continuous screen-filling level.
Primary request: make the already active station recognize a person through LCL. Show changed access and attention with minimal effects that remain legible at game scale.
Changes: the waiting adult takes a short step toward the existing relay on the pier and raises an open hand quietly near it, retaining the small tool bag in the other hand. Keep this a compact character sprite with realistic proportions. The existing gate panels swing physically open, showing a continuous walkable passage through their existing housings. The wall dispenser's delivery hatch opens with a small plain cup visibly inside. The freight crane's existing sensor head turns toward the adult and relay while the crane and cargo stay in position. Existing small terminal, gate, and sensor indicators become coordinated pale cyan/amber accents; tiny existing status symbols show permitted passage. Keep indicator glow confined to their hardware.
Human residents: the repairer remains at the same upper-left workbench and the seated person stays with their tea at the lower-left bench. Preserve all fitted repairs, domestic details, and maintenance boundaries.
Priority: this is LCL as recognition and accommodation, not a spell. The visibly open gate and responding sensor do most of the work. Keep the same scene lighting, contact shadows, material palette, and disciplined surface detail. No change of weather, zoom, orientation, or terrain.
Avoid: floating interface, energy beams, magic circles, aura around the person, glowing veins, particles, lightning, bloom, dramatic new lighting, neon wash, extra giant robots, new people, photographic lens effects, horizon, miniature island display, UI, captions, labels, borders, logos, or watermark.
